primary_claim: Adding factored cognition (task decomposition with isolated child-task contexts) to a trusted monitoring AI control protocol boosts safety on the APPS backdoor red-teaming setting from 41% to 70%, driven in part by improved monitor performance at recognizing attacks on simpler child tasks, and drops attack success rate from 26% to 14%.

effect.metric: safety (%) on APPS red-teaming; attack success rate (%)
effect.value: safety 41% (trusted monitoring baseline) to 70% (Factor(D,U)); attack success rate 26% to 14%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Notes that the red team's ability to model the trusted monitor reached an unusually high correlation (r=0.69) in an earlier setup, exceeding the max r=0.45 found by the low-stakes control paper (Greenblatt et al.), but this correlation disappeared with their final model selection

Qualifies the field's use of APPS as a control setting by arguing it cannot give a unified safety/usefulness comparison of decomposition protocols against simple baselines because the needed model-selection criteria (capability gap + low decomposition tax) are jointly unsatisfiable on APPS
stated_future_work: Develop a new, more difficult control setting (e.g. an LLM agent setting with multi-step attacks) to properly benchmark factored cognition protocols
Test the product-threat vs process-threat hypothesis using two matched evals
Build a unified benchmark/evaluation framework for task decomposition capability across models, datasets, and scaffolds
Extend Factor(T,U) with other implementers, additional monitoring/editing steps, unit-test generation, and dynamic/deep decomposition trees
Red-team Factor(U,T) and Factor(U,U) protocols, including studying steganographic collusion bandwidth between decomposer and implementers
limitations_stated: Did not work as hard on decomposer elicitation and prompt engineering as the original AI control paper (Greenblatt et al. 2023)
Used a powerful decomposer (o3-mini) rather than the weak trusted model T, biasing usefulness comparisons between decomposition and non-decomposition protocols to the point of invalidity
The APPS setting is inadequate: model-selection criteria (capability gap and low decomposition tax) cannot jointly be satisfied, and the benchmark is already close to saturation
All reported results are on the train split; the held-out test split has not yet been used
The reduced attack success rate under factored cognition is only weak evidence for the 'security through obscurity' hypothesis since exploit-finder capability could be a confounding bottleneck
quote: Adding factored cognition to a trusted monitoring protocol boosts safety from 41% to 70% due in part to improved monitor performance.
